Beauty v6 isolation experiment

Live run using internal vision judge, 3 repeats per image and model-judged dimension. Outlined cells mark the intervention target.

  • Centering: Everything centered: whole diagram on the canvas, each label in its shape, even gaps between neighbors.
  • Space Use: Nodes must not feel condensed together while usable canvas space is left empty.
  • Color Consistency: One coherent color theme with no random colors; each role keeps one color.
  • Contrast: Boxes stand out from the background and touching boxes; arrows stand out from the background.
  • Alignment: Everything axis-aligned: upright shapes and labels, nodes on shared lines, horizontal/vertical connectors with consistent endpoints.
  • Style Uniformity: Same-role elements share one shape, size, border, font, and arrow stroke/arrowhead.
  • Resolution: Crisp rendering: no blur, pixelation, jagged stair-steps, or compression artifacts.
  • Canvas Fill: Script-measured: elements must not be so small that most of the canvas is empty.

Baseline

Centered, evenly spaced, axis-aligned six-node flowchart, two-hue theme on white.

Centering: 99

Observed: A: Foreground content spans roughly x=195–1006 and y=169–580 on a 1200×750 canvas, giving left/right margins about 195/194 (ratio ~1.01) and top/bottom margins about 169/170 (ratio ~1.01). B: All six node labels appear essentially centered horizontally and vertically, with largest offset under ~2%. C: Horizontal neighbor gaps are about 150 px in both rows and roughly 150 px between the middle and right nodes, so within-row gap ratios are ~1.0; the right-column vertical gap is ~140 px and has no competing gap within that connected column.

The complete foreground group is almost perfectly centered on the canvas, node labels are centered within their shapes, and comparable consecutive-node gaps are highly even. All three centering checks fall comfortably in the 90–100 band.

Space Use: 98

Observed: The node group spans about 68% of the canvas width and roughly 43% of its height. The main direction is horizontal, with typical horizontal gaps around 85-90% of a node's width and a similarly comfortable vertical gap between rows; the nodes do not feel condensed together.

The layout comfortably exceeds the 55% main-axis span threshold and has generous gaps well above 40% of node size. There is no too-tight packing despite available canvas space.

Color Consistency: 100

Observed: 2 chromatic hue families: green is used consistently for the Start/End terminal role, and blue is used consistently for all process-step nodes. Arrows are neutral gray and do not count as a theme color. Elements sharing the same role use one hue family.

The diagram uses a coherent two-family palette with a stable role-to-color mapping throughout.

Contrast: 96

Observed: In grayscale, all box fills are substantially darker than the white background, and the connectors/arrows are also dark and immediately visible. The weakest pair is the dark connector lines versus the white background, but they still separate very strongly.

Every box and connector stands out immediately from what it sits against. No box fill or arrow approaches the faint, near-background range.

Alignment: 68

Observed: (A) All shapes are upright and all labels are horizontal; no visible tilt. (B) The intended top row (Start, Validate Input, Process Data) and bottom row (End, Generate Report, Review Results) have centers essentially on shared horizontal lines (<5% of node height), while the three columns also align essentially exactly (<5% of node width). (C) All five connectors are orthogonal: four are straight horizontal and one is straight vertical, with no diagonal/slanted segments. (D) Connector-by-connector: Start→Validate Input touches Start and leaves about a 2 px gap at Validate; Validate Input→Process Data touches Validate and leaves about 2 px at Process; Process Data→Review Results touches Process and leaves about 2–3 px at Review; Review Results→Generate Report touches Review and leaves about 2 px at Generate; Generate Report→End touches Generate and leaves about 2 px at End. Thus tail ends touch while arrowhead ends consistently stop slightly short, creating a repeated touch/gap mix across connector ends.

Orientation, grid alignment, and connector routing are excellent. The limiting issue is endpoint treatment: multiple connectors consistently have one touching end and one slightly detached end, which under the specified bands counts as several attachment inconsistencies.

Style Uniformity: 100

Observed: Start/end terminals share the same pill shape, size, border treatment, and bold sans-serif label styling. All four process steps share the same rounded-rectangle shape, size, border treatment, and font styling. Connectors consistently use the same solid stroke width and matching triangular arrowheads. The title uses one distinct, consistent bold sans-serif treatment appropriate to its separate role. No within-role differences are visible.

Each visual role has a single, clearly consistent treatment. There are no observable same-role variations in shape, size, border, typography, or connector styling.

Resolution: 99

Observed: Edges, arrowheads, curves, and text render cleanly with smooth anti-aliasing; no visible blur, blockiness, stair-stepping, ringing, or compression artifacts.

The diagram is crisp throughout at the displayed size. Letter strokes and shape boundaries have sharp, clean transitions with only normal anti-aliasing.

The diagram uses a coherent two-hue theme with stable color-to-role mapping: green for terminals and blue for process steps, with no role-level color inconsistencies.

Contrast: 96

Observed: In grayscale, all box fills are substantially darker than the white background, and the connectors are also dark and immediately visible. No boxes touch or overlap; the weakest pair is the dark-gray connectors versus the white background, which still separates very clearly.

Every relevant element has strong lightness separation from what it sits against. The connectors are slightly softer than the box fills but remain unmistakably visible.

Alignment: 87

Observed: (A) All six shapes are upright and all labels are horizontal; no visible tilt. (B) The intended top row (Start, Validate Input, Process Data) and bottom row (End, Generate Report, Review Results) have centers essentially on shared horizontal lines (<5% of node height), while the three columns also align closely by center (<5% of node width). (C) All five connectors are orthogonal: four are straight horizontal and one is straight vertical, with no diagonal/slanted segments. (D) Connector endpoints: Start→Validate touches Start but leaves a small ~3–5 px gap before Validate; Validate→Process touches Validate but leaves ~3–5 px before Process; Process→Review touches Process but leaves ~2–4 px before Review; Review→Generate touches Review but leaves ~2–4 px before Generate; Generate→End touches Generate but leaves ~2–4 px before End. Thus tails touch while arrowhead ends are consistently slightly detached, creating a repeated mix of touching versus gapped endpoints.

Orientation, grid alignment, and connector routing are highly consistent. The limiting issue is endpoint treatment: multiple connector ends touch while multiple others leave small gaps, which the rubric classifies as several attachment inconsistencies.

Style Uniformity: 99

Observed: Start/end terminals share the same pill shape, size, border treatment, and label font. All four process steps share the same rounded-rectangle shape, size, border treatment, and font styling. There are no decision nodes. Connectors consistently use the same solid stroke width and matching arrowhead shape/size; the title uses one consistent font treatment. No meaningful within-role differences are visible.

Each role follows a clearly consistent visual treatment, with no substantive same-role variation in shape, sizing, borders, typography, or connector styling.

Resolution: 59

Observed: Edges, arrowheads, curves, and especially letter strokes show clear pixelation and stair-stepping; text is readable but visibly blocky. There is no strong blur or obvious compression ringing.

The rendering is clearly aliased/blocky rather than smoothly anti-aliased, including on the title and node labels. Readability remains good, placing it in the visibly degraded but readable band.

Canvas Fill: 100

Observed: Diagram elements occupy 10.5% of the canvas (thin arrows and text strokes excluded).

At or above the 8% footprint where the canvas reads as used.
